name: The Butts and the Briar
description: Fernhold eats because Rosen Wyke shoots. She teaches the bow at the butts behind the lodge, walks you along the Briar with her father while he counts the grey, and puts you on the lip over Wold Force at evening, when the thornhounds come down to drink.
notes: The ranger's tutorial (docs/FIGHTING_STYLE_STARTS.md 3.2, 3.2a), begun by core:opening/ranger. The butts are Pell bodies of kind butt (QuestSpots `props`), 20, 35 and 50 m down the range from the shooting line; the weaver is one of Fern Gully's own; the thornhounds are Wold Force's own three, and Rosen shoots only if you are hurt (`overwatch`, Sparring's sibling in Overwatch). Rosen's and Alder's lines are in their dialogues and hold them at the butts, the Briar and the lip (their npc defs' holds).

stages.journal: Across Fernhold's common, from the antler hall's end to the wood's edge, the lodge keeps a range: three straw butts on trestles at twenty, thirty-five and fifty paces from the line. Rosen Wyke says: draw, hold, and loose on the out-breath. A held draw costs you stamina for as long as you hold it, so do not stand there admiring yourself. The further the butt, the more the arrow falls on the way: aim over the far one.

objectives.text: Hit the near butt: draw with {key:attack_light}, hold, let go

say: Breathe out. Loose on the empty. The arrow doesn't care how brave you are.

objectives.text: Hit the middle butt at thirty-five paces

say: It dropped. They all drop. Aim where it's going to be, not where it is.

objectives.text: Hit the far butt at fifty paces: aim over it

say: Good. Go and pull them out of the straw. Arrows are a thing that runs out. Then we walk the Briar with my father.

stages.journal: Alder Wyke walks the Briar every morning, the wall of thorn the Oroth grew to keep the Hush in the south, and counts the grey patches in it. Rosen takes you with him. Go quietly: crouched, you are harder to see and harder to hear, and the Wold has more ears than the Rest has Wardens. Walk into the wind, so what is ahead of you cannot smell you coming. Find them out on the Briar's edge north-west of the lodge.

objectives.text: Find Alder Wyke on the Briar, and watch him count

stages.journal: Beyond the grey patch the path goes down into Fern Gully, where the woodfolk have hung plank bridges between the trunks and something else has hung other things. A weaver drops from the canopy on anything that walks under it. Rosen says a ranger does not stand under things: when it drops, back off or roll clear, and shoot it while it is still on the ground working out where you went.

objectives.text: Put down a weaver in Fern Gully

say: Don't chase it. Let it come round. Everything comes round.

stages.journal: Wold Force falls into a pool a long bowshot south of the lodge, and the thornhounds come down to drink at it, three of them, every evening. Rosen puts you on the high ground over the pool, on its east side, with the wind in your face. Shoot from up there before they find you. If one closes, take the knife into your hand and roll back to where the bow is some use again. She will not shoot unless you are hurt.

objectives.text: Put down the thornhounds at Wold Force
Hit them from the high ground, before they find you
When one closes, take the knife into your hand {key:quick_4}

stages.journal: The pool is quiet again. Go back to the lodge with Rosen. She has something to say about it, and she will say less than she means.

objectives.text: Walk back to Fernhold with Rosen

name: The Grey Hart
description: The hart whose slots you read on the Briar has gone grey, and it is walking south out of the wood, and it does not run from you. Alder Wyke knows where it is going and wants to be wrong.
notes: The ranger's tie-in (docs/FIGHTING_STYLE_STARTS.md 3.2, 3.2a): the hart is a lead (Leads) that keeps ahead of the player by road, the recommended ride that does not touch the Standing Moot, by Grandfather Hollow and Tamwick; a Hearthstone halfway at Ansel's Hedge Shrine; a thornhound pack at Tamwick, come south after the hart (QuestFoes); and the Stair Head, where the hart walks past the Warden's fire and down the stair, and the Naming begins at down_the_stair.

stages.journal: At first light the hart whose slots you read on the Briar was standing at the edge of the lodge's clearing, and it had gone grey: not the grey of a hart's winter coat, the grey of a thing with the colour taken out. It looked at the lodge the way a thing looks at somewhere it used to live. It did not run. Alder is watching it from the hall. Speak to him.

objectives.text: Speak to Alder about the grey hart

stages.journal: Alder wants you to follow the hart and find where it goes, because he knows where it goes and he wants to be wrong. It walks south by the road, as if it had read the fingerposts, and it keeps a field ahead of you however you come on. Rosen's pony knows the roads. Follow it to Grandfather Hollow, and on.

objectives.text: Follow the grey hart south to Grandfather Hollow

stages.journal: The hart went round the Standing Moot, where the Hart of Thorns stands in the stones, and did not look at it, and then down off the Wold towards Tamwick. Behind it on the road came three thornhounds out of the Briar. They are not after the hart. They are going the same way, and you are in it.

objectives.text: Put down the thornhounds on the Tamwick road

stages.journal: Halfway, a little off the road west of Tamwick, is Ansel's Hedge Shrine, and a Hearthstone in its lee. Put your hand on it and say your name, so that if the road kills you it knows where to give you back. The hart waited on the road while you did, which a hart does not do.

objectives.text: Turn off to Ansel's Hedge Shrine
Put your hand on the shrine's Hearthstone

stages.journal: Through the Vale, by Merrowby with its bell humming in the hole, by Wynstead and Ashwell to Pilgrim's Ash, and south past the Choir's twelve headless colossi to a camp on a cliff's edge, where a woman in a grey-green cloak keeps a fire at the top of a stair. The hart has stopped at the camp's edge. It is waiting, and it is looking at the stair.

objectives.text: Speak to the Warden at the Stair Head

say: Don't. It's not yours to stop. — It's going down. It's going down! Nobody comes back up!
